New studies have brought to light the impact of global climate change, which is projected to reduce future crop yields and thus
threaten food security and eliminate much of the improvement in child undernutrition levels that would occur with no climate
change. It has been estimated that climate change would lead to a relative increase in moderate stunting of 1–29% in 2050
compared to a future without climate change. Climate change would have a greater impact on severe stunting rates, projected to
increase by 23% (central sub-Saharan Africa) to 62% (South Asia). Moreover, losses would be exacerbated by the additional
loss of food post-harvest due to bad storage conditions as well as inadequate systems of food distribution, thus also contributing
to the development of undernutrition, even after periods of agricultural abundance.
